scope: Partial results for exact plane branch-integrality optimization and specified surface subclasses; no complete resolution of the original geometric hypothesis question.
main_results: For a smooth irreducible plane branch of degree b, the minimum absolute twist over all positive symmetric orders is b+1.
For any effective reduced nonempty plane branch divisor of degree b, exact minimum absolute twist is computed by testing 2<=k<=b+1 and 1<=r<=floor(k/2).
The universal normalized-twist minimum is 2; all threshold forms have a complete dual-polynomial description.
Conic-tangent line arrangements of at least five lines have global minimum absolute twist 4; this is compared with established cyclic-cover applications.
Pencil base-change constructions give explicit smooth generically finite surface classes, with essential exceptional corrections and complete genus-bounded conclusions.
A specified verified nef/ramification budget gives a finite differential-existence test; positivity verification and arbitrary integral-curve completeness remain separate.
limitations: Code implements rational coefficients only; effectiveness over algebraic coefficients is proved but not implemented.
No general algorithm for the needed upstairs positivity cone or all integral curves is claimed.
The pencil base-change morphism to the plane is generally not finite.
Existing transfer theorems and conic-tangent cyclic-cover applications are credited; no new priority claim.
